title: A Rock 150 Feet Wide Hit Arizona at 26,000 mph. The Hole Is Still There

scenes.text: A rock 150 feet wide hit Arizona at 26,000 miles an hour.
Fifty thousand years ago. A lump of iron and nickel.
It hit with the force of ten million tons of TNT. About 600 Hiroshima bombs, in one instant.
Boulders the size of houses landed a mile away.
The iron mostly vaporised. A mining engineer drilled for 26 years looking for it. Nothing.
The hole is three quarters of a mile wide and 560 feet deep. Apollo astronauts trained in it.
scenes.keywords: Meteor Crater rim tourists looking down

description:
Meteor Crater in Arizona was blasted out about 50,000 years ago by an iron-nickel meteorite roughly 150 feet across travelling around 26,000 miles an hour.
The impact released at least 10 megatons of energy, threw out 175 million tons of rock and left a hole three quarters of a mile wide and about 560 feet deep. Daniel Barringer drilled for 26 years looking for the iron mass, which had largely vaporised on impact.
Would you stand on the rim? Comment below.
first_comment: The crater was originally about 700 feet deep; 50,000 years of wind and rain have half filled it. Would you rather it had landed in the ocean or the desert?
